I am 65 years old and I have farmed this land since I was a young girl. My mother and father taught me everything I know about growing maize. I do not have cash to buy chemical fertilizer from the agro-dealer — one bag costs too much for my small plot and I would not even use it all. I will spread manure from our compound instead, it costs nothing and it has always kept the soil good enough. I will plant the seed I saved from last harvest, not those new seeds they sell in town that need fertilizer to grow well. I will pull the weeds with my hands when they come up, and if the pests arrive I will pick them off, I do not spray chemicals. The rain will come when God sends it, I have no water for irrigation. My children and grandchildren will help me when they can, and I will work slowly every day — maybe three weeks of work altogether over the season. I cannot pay hired workers, we will do it ourselves with our own hands.
